pr_title: specify a custom web browser to launch
pr_body:
instead of launching the default browser, pass a custom file path.

also include a string-wrapped csv of command line flags like "incognito,start-maximized"
Fixes #1409

issue_context.title: allow custom browser instead of default
issue_context.body:
Pass in a custom path to run as the browser on startup instead of using the default:

--custom-browser-path "C:\Program Files\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\Application\brave.exe" --custom-browser-args-csv "start-maximized,incognito"
comments:
I'm not saying this isn't a legitimate ask, but...

1) the operating system has domain over application defaults including default browser.

2) beyond that the comfyui frontend actually works in a 'supported' set of browsers, it's really out of scope. Being able to override the browser at the application level makes sense when the application is directly related to the operation of the browser. I'm thinking of Selenium UI Test Driver.

3) you can invert the responsibility and instead of telling comfy to open browser X, you launch comfy with browser X: `firefox.exe --url 0.0.0.0:8188`. Also use `--auto-launch false` in the comfy command.

review_comments: Is there a reason to do this whole thing, vs just `--custom-browser-args "--incognito --etc --etc"`?
In my experience the parser couldn't handle it, but I'm not a python developer
